dataset.provider: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal (CCKP)
dataset.geography: Philippines (ISO3 PHL), country mean, spatial aggregation 'mean'
dataset.projection_product: CMIP6 0.25-degree multi-model ensemble climatology, scenario SSP2-4.5
dataset.rcp_equivalence: SSP2-4.5 carries the same 4.5 W/m2 end-of-century forcing level as CMIP5 RCP4.5 and is used here as the requested RCP4.5-equivalent pathway. This mirrors the choice already made for Fiji_v2.6 in scripts/data/fiji_v26_precipitation_ssp245.json.

observed_annual_mm_per_year.source: ERA5-x0.25 historical annual timeseries, country mean
observed_annual_mm_per_year.note: CCKP returns annual values keyed 'YYYY-07' (July midpoint convention). Keys below are calendar years. 2024 and 2025 draw on ERA5T preliminary input and should be treated as provisional.

historical_climatology_median_mm_per_yea.note: CMIP6 ensemble median for the reference period. It sits 9.4 percent below the ERA5 1995-2014 observed mean of 2735.3 mm/yr, which is why anomalies (not absolute projected climatologies) are the quantity carried into the model.

seasonal_anomaly_mm_per_season_median.note: Season keys follow the CCKP convention: 01 = DJF, 04 = MAM, 07 = JJA, 10 = SON.
seasonal_anomaly_mm_per_season_median.interpretation: The wet seasons gain 38-41 mm by 2040-2059 while MAM (March-May, the pre-monsoon dry season that sets irrigation and hydropower stress) gains essentially nothing. Annual-mean wetting therefore does not imply dry-season relief.

derived_multipliers_relative_to_1995_201.formula: multiplier = 1 + CCKP median annual anomaly / CCKP 1995-2014 historical climatology median
derived_multipliers_relative_to_1995_201.annualisation: Linear interpolation 2020 -> 2030 anchor, then 2030 -> 2050 anchor, then held on the same slope to 2053 (model horizon).

national_water_resources.note: Reference values for national potential sensitivities. These are national assessment figures, not model outputs, dependable flow, environmental-flow-adjusted availability, groundwater safe yield, or aquifer stock.
sources: National Water Resources Board figures as reported in the Philippine Department of Economy, Planning and Development (formerly NEDA) Policy Note on the Philippine Water Sector, https://depdev.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Policy-Note-on-the-Philippine-Water-Sector.pdf

Philippine Statistics Authority, water use efficiency and water stress release (SDG 6.4.1 / 6.4.2), https://psa.gov.ph/content/countrys-overall-water-use-efficiency-decreased-while-water-stress-remains-low-level

groundwater_evidence.model_role: The currently available evidence supports an annual national renewable-flow sensitivity and local screening only. It does not support initialization of aquifer stock, drawdown, or depletion.
groundwater_evidence.historical_regional_source: PIDS Development Research News regional water-resource table; use as an older planning cross-check only, https://pidswebs.pids.gov.ph/CDN/PUBLICATIONS/pidsdrn11-3.pdf

local_study_leads.Cebu_note: Local recharge constraints and saltwater-intrusion risk; do not extrapolate nationally.
local_study_leads.source: PIDS, Metro Manila and Metro Cebu Groundwater Assessment, https://serp-p.pids.gov.ph/publication/public/view?slug=metro-manila-and-metro-cebu-groundwater-assessment

groundwater_evidence.spatial_screening_source: MGB Regional Groundwater Availability feature layer; categorical screening, not a volumetric stock or safe-yield dataset, https://controlmap.mgb.gov.ph/arcgis/rest/services/GeospatialDataInventory/GDI_Regional_Groundwater_Availability/FeatureServer/0
required_for_aquifer_stock: aquifer polygons crosswalked to land clusters and demand nodes
initial saturated thickness or head and reference date
aquifer area and specific yield or storage coefficient
precipitation-to-recharge calibration by aquifer, season, land cover, soil, and geology
natural discharge, baseflow, and groundwater-dependent ecosystem requirements
pumping locations, lift and energy, salinity and critical-area limits
observed head time series for validation

spatial_data_status.national_model_requirement: No cluster geometry is required for the proposed whole-country formulation. All eight LNDAGRPHLC classes feed shared national surface-water and groundwater commodities and receive the same national climate multiplier.
spatial_data_status.retained_companion_artifacts: EAPD-DRB/CLEWs-PHL retains the national boundary, a cluster-map PNG, and eight-row land-cover, parameter, precipitation, evapotranspiration and crop-water-deficit summaries that reproduce the model coefficients, https://github.com/EAPD-DRB/CLEWs-PHL/tree/main/Philippines_v12_CLEWs_build/geospatial
spatial_data_status.missing_optional_artifact: Cell-level cluster geometry or point membership is absent. This matters only for a future spatial rebuild with basin/aquifer commodities, geographically allocated demands and explicit transfers; it does not block a national water balance or national withdrawal ceiling.

limitations: The CCKP ensemble climatologies are period means represented by their midpoints. The year-by-year interpolation is a modelling assumption, not an annual forecast.

Only the ensemble median is proposed for installation in the model. p10 and p90 are retained as research metadata, not predefined model scenarios; note that p10 is drier than the 1995-2014 reference in both periods, so the sign of the change is not robust.
ERA5 is a reanalysis, not a gauge network. It is used here for a consistent 76-year national mean; PAGASA station data remain the authority for Philippine station-level rainfall.
The 2024 and 2025 ERA5 values rely on ERA5T preliminary input and may be revised.
Anomalies are national means. They do not represent the eight spatial clusters of the land block separately, nor typhoon rainfall, El Nino/La Nina sequencing, or interannual variability.

The national water resource figures are potential and withdrawal assessments from national sources. They are not derived from the model's own runoff coefficients and are not a sustainable-yield calculation for any specific basin or aquifer.
The 20.2 km3/year groundwater figure is an annual national potential flow, not an aquifer volume or stock initial condition.
The current MUIO formulation fixes StorageLevelYearStart to zero in every year and cannot carry groundwater stock or depletion across model years.

The eight land clusters are coefficient classes feeding shared national water pools, not river basins or aquifers. The national proposal intentionally applies one climate path and national withdrawal ceilings; it makes no local-scarcity claim.
